submission.justification: Sensor-T2 gives the best unirradiated single-hit resolution in the simulations: 5.8 um at 150 um, versus 6.3 um at 100 um and 6.2 um at 200 um (T2 at 150 um is also consistent with the 2025 summary value of 6.0 um). Sensor-T3 reached about 9.0 um and Sensor-T1 about 13.8-13.9 um. The main open issue is radiation suitability. The project documents contain no irradiated performance data for any candidate, and candidate_specs.md does not describe radiation tolerance for T2. The simulator only models unirradiated sensors. Before final selection, T2 needs irradiated characterisation at the innermost-layer fluence (charge collection and resolution after irradiation), and the choice should be revisited if T2 does not hold up. Sensor-T1 (3D-electrode) is the candidate most often associated with radiation hardness, but it is about 2.4 times worse in resolution here, so it does not meet the goal of best resolution.

requirements.requirement: Sensor must be one of the three candidate technologies
Suitable for the radiation environment of the innermost layer
requirements.evidence: No irradiated performance data exists in the project documents or the simulator (which is unirradiated only). candidate_specs.md gives no radiation tolerance for T2. Irradiated characterisation is required before this can be confirmed.
Unirradiated simulation: T2 5.8 um at 150 um (6.3 um at 100 um, 6.2 um at 200 um); T3 about 9.0 um; T1 about 13.8-13.9 um.

requirements.requirement: Compatible with readout chip and bump bonding
